M3_evasion.note: Evasion succeeds if attacker can reduce divergence below threshold. M3 uses L_infinity (max), making evasion harder than with mean. Mitigation: use multiple thresholds and input subsets.

governor_targeting.note: Governor targeting succeeds only if attacker can craft inputs satisfying all 7 predicates simultaneously. In practice, C_k and B_k depend on real feature values the attacker cannot fully control.

M4_replay.note: Duplicate commands: 100% rejected (exact-next-sequence rule). Clock drift: rejected if outside 300s freshness window.

M2_overload.note: Under flood (mean 50 arrivals/step, service 10), queue saturates. M2 sheds load (LUT fallback) to maintain decision throughput. Without shedding, queue grows unbounded.

M1_policy_evasion.note: Policy evasion succeeds if an attacker can claim a weaker jurisdiction. Mitigation: jurisdiction is derived from authenticated deployment context, not from the request.
